extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners developing or evaluating automatic scientific peer-review generation systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, training, and evaluating automatic systems that generate peer reviews for scientific papers, including dataset construction, extraction strategies, aspect-aware generation, automatic and human evaluation, and bias analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desiderata of reviews (Decisive, Comprehensiveness, Justification, Accuracy, Others)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of high-level desiderata that good reviews should satisfy, listed in the paper (figure/table): Decisive; Comprehensiveness; Justification; Accuracy; Others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These desiderata are the target qualities the review-generation system aims to realize (the paper evaluates systems with respect to these desiderata using concrete metrics described elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect categories (MOT, ORI, SOU, SUB, REP, CLA, CMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-grained aspect taxonomy used to annotate and evaluate reviews: MOT (Motivation), ORI (Originality), SOU (Soundness), SUB (Substance), REP (Replicability), CLA (Clarity), CMP (Meaningful Comparison).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each generated or human review is evaluated on these aspects (polarity/constructiveness per aspect via an aspect tagger). Aspects are used for Aspect Coverage, Aspect Recall, aspect-level constructiveness, and bias analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect Coverage (ACOV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic evaluation metric measuring coverage of annotated aspects in a generated review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspect information for references obtained via aspect tagger (§3.2). When aggregating across multiple reference reviews for a source, aggregate ACOV by averaging for each source document (the paper notes averaging for 'other metrics' for human reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect Recall (AREC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic evaluation metric measuring recall of aspects present in reference reviews that are covered by generated reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed using the annotated aspects and tagger outputs; aggregated per-source (averaging across references for human review metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic equivalence (ROUGE)
rubrics_metrics.description: ROUGE family of metrics to evaluate semantic/content overlap between generated reviews and reference reviews (used as a semantic equivalence measure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each source input with multiple reference reviews, aggregate ROUGE by taking the maximum score across references (not the average). ROUGE is used both for oracle extraction construction and final automatic evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic equivalence (BERTScore)
rubrics_metrics.description: BERTScore as a learned semantic similarity measure between generated and reference reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors use a custom baseline to rescale BERTScore (see Appendix). For multiple references, aggregate by taking the maximum across references. BERTScore appears in automated metric tables as 'BS'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation Accuracy (RACC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human evaluation metric measuring whether the generated review's recommendation (e.g., accept/reject) matches reference/human recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via human judgments on a held-out set of papers (28 papers from ML/NLP/CV/RL domains). The paper reports large performance gaps between systems and humans on RACC (e.g., smallest gap observed 41.86%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informativeness (INFO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human evaluation metric assessing how informative a review is (how much useful information it conveys about the paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via human raters; systems in some cases outperform human reviewers on informativeness (up to 2.03% in reported experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect-level Constructiveness (ACON)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human evaluation metric measuring constructiveness at the aspect level (does the review give constructive, actionable feedback per aspect?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems performed much worse than human reviewers on ACON (large absolute gaps, e.g., ~31.89% in reported comparisons). Focus on improving constructiveness is recommended over simply improving evidence quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Accuracy (SACC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human evaluation metric measuring whether the generated review correctly summarizes the paper's contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by humans; several systems achieved over 80% SACC, and gaps between top systems and human reviewers were not statistically significant in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asking Questions (question-count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic criterion counting the number of questions posed in a review as a component of peer reviewing (reflects interrogative engagement with the paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference reviews average 2.04 questions per review while generated reviews average 0.32, indicating generated reviews ask far fewer questions — use question count as a constructiveness/engagement signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factuality and Reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Desideratum that generated reviews should be factually correct and provide reliable claims about paper content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factuality is challenging to evaluate; the paper highlights the need for evaluation methodologies that measure factual correctness and proposes that reliable systems should also provide confidence estimates for assertions in reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring bias in reviews (aspect score, disparity δ, disparity difference Δ and visualization)
rubrics_metrics.description: A procedure for identifying and quantifying biases in human and system-generated reviews using fine-grained aspects: (i) aspect score AS(R,Gi) = percentage of positive occurrences of each aspect in group Gi; (ii) disparity δ(R,G) = AS(R,G0) − AS(R,G1); (iii) disparity difference Δ(Rg, Rr, G) = δ(Rg,G) − δ(Rr,G). Visualized with spider charts and reported as disparity differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polarity per aspect obtained from a learned aspect tagger (§3.2). If an aspect does not appear in a review, count its score as 0.5 (neutral). Grouping examples include nativeness (native vs non-native) and anonymity (anonymous vs non-anonymous). Positive Δ means generated reviews favor group G0 more than reference reviews. Tabulate total bias as sum of absolute disparity differences per aspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation rules for multiple reference reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for aggregating metrics when multiple reference reviews exist for a single source document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ROUGE and BERTScore, take the maximum across references for a given source input. For other metrics (e.g., human-review-aggregated metrics like ACOV when computed over human reviews), take the average per source document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oracle extraction (greedy oracle maximizing ROUGE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oracle extraction: construct, for each paper (and for each reference review when multiple exist), the extraction that achieves the highest average ROUGE with respect to reference reviews using a greedy method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oracle extractions are used as an upper-bound/analysis tool to reflect where reviewers pay attention. Multiple oracles per paper when multiple references exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraction strategy: Input scope (introduction vs full paper) and truncation
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of source text used for extraction (introduction-only vs full paper) and truncation policy: if a paper has more than 250 sentences, take the first 250 sentences for extraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using extracted text from the full paper is more effective (higher aspect coverage) than using only the introduction. Filter out papers with full text <100 words for dataset construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset filters and review length constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset construction constraints: only include papers with full text ≥100 words and use reviews between 100–1024 words for training (these account for 92.57% of reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These thresholds were applied for computational efficiency and quality of training data; result was ~8,742 unique papers and 25,986 paper-review pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation constraints for produced reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Decoding and generation constraints used when producing reviews: beam search with beam size 4, minimum length 100 tokens, maximum length 1024 tokens, length penalty 2.0, trigram blocking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These hyperparameters were used during generation; different pretraining checkpoints (e.g., 'bart-large-cnn' vs 'bart-large-xsum') can affect generated review length and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model initialization and training protocol (practical production standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical setup used for training: initialize seq2seq model with 'bart-large-cnn' checkpoint; added MLP initialized with mean 0 and std 0.02; Adam optimizer with linear learning-rate scheduler warming up to 4e-5 over first 10% of steps then linear decay; fine-tune for 5 epochs and select checkpoint with lowest validation loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These choices represent recommended/used settings in experiments. For aspect-aware multitask model, total loss L = L_seq2seq + α L_seqlab with α = 0.1 tuned to maximize aspect coverage on development set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance testing for metric differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Method for testing whether differences between system-generated and human reviews are statistically significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 10,000 paired bootstrap resampling (Efron, 1992) tests with 0.8 sample ratio; report differences as statistically significant at p < 0.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitating style / n-gram frequency bias diagnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: An observed failure mode: models may imitate frequent sentence-level patterns from training data (e.g., 'The paper is well-written and easy to follow' appearing >90% of generated reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use diagnostics to detect overuse of high-frequency sentence patterns; indicates lack of diversity and overfitting to stylistic artifacts in data.
